reason: The active NN assembly spends substantial work packing A: its packing loop loads many vectors, moves them through ZA, then stores the packed data. A 32-row panel directly targets that work, though its assembly changes carry correctness risk. Vectorizing Strassen packing is a smaller, testable target, but the compiler may already vectorize it. The measured three-buffer Strassen wrapper lost all ten paired runs, so removing its output-zero pass ranks ahead of allocation or product-buffer changes only as a limited follow-up; none addresses the whole regression. The K-loop decrement and branch are visible, but replacing them with flag-setting decrement and conditional branch does not reduce instruction count, so benefit is uncertain. Transpose fusion rereads A sixteen times, and tail handling does not affect n=512 timing. These are unverified rankings, not performance predictions. The supplied board contains eight experiment IDs; each is listed once.
